desc:
This presentation will focus on real-world examples from an enterprise IPv6 address plan, taking time to review the principles of proper address planning for the existing corporate IT network as well as exploring options for addressing emerging network technologies like IoT, containerization/microservices, and cloud.

recs.x:
I would recommend you check out Tom Coffeen, who wrote a book on IPv6 address planning for O'Reilly. Even with half the bits going to the subnet, there is a astronomical amount of addresses available:

* [link]

This talk[0] is an hour long but from 22:18 on they discuss their recommended IPV6 address plan (the whole video really opened my eyes to IPV6 and made it all much more understandable). You shouldn’t subdivide below /64, as RFC 5375[1] does not recommend it and as discussed here[2] there are some pitfalls you can encounter.
